title: From Inertia to Objectivity: Improving Deep Research Agents with Noise Isolation

visual_explainer.question: Can a search agent judge new evidence more objectively when its self-authored trajectory is removed from the decision context?
visual_explainer.takeaway: Worker-side observation isolation separates page triage from prior narration, while manager-side validation rebuilds cited inference steps before deciding to stop.
visual_explainer.compared_with: The same task and returned search results presented inside the agent-authored trajectory rather than observer context.

analysis.tldr: NIS-Agent tests whether self-authored search history biases later evidence judgment. In IBIS, showing the same task and returned results in observer rather than agent-owned context improves re-search decisions by roughly 15–30 points; the full package also improves GAIA/WebWalkerQA while reducing GPT-4o tokens from 219.8K to 147.3K. Package attribution and complete tool/call accounting remain incomplete.
analysis.problem: A deep-research agent can become anchored to its own earlier narration, treating a weak page as sufficient or validating a flawed inference because it appears inside a self-authored trajectory.
analysis.core_idea: Reconstruct a compact worker context that contains the task, current query, and returned results without trajectory ownership, then let a manager reorganize the final trace into independently checked cited inference steps before stopping.
analysis.agent_loop: search results → ownership-isolated page triage → browse or re-search → cited inference reconstruction → local validation → correct or stop
analysis.retrieval_design: IBIS locally matches task and observations while changing ownership framing. End-to-end comparisons use the same backbone and a smolagents-derived harness, but filter, validation, and some integrated tools move together.
compared_to: Agentic Mode versus Observer Mode on IBIS
analysis.evidence: Observer Mode raises Should-Re-search accuracy by about 15–30 points across most IBIS models. With GPT-4o, GAIA rises 54.88 to 61.82 and WebWalkerQA 46.50 to 57.50; GAIA tokens fall from 219.8K to 147.3K.
analysis.why_it_matters: It makes context ownership and validation delivery part of the retrieval harness, showing that identical observations can produce different search decisions depending on how prior agent state is presented.
limitations: The end-to-end package changes filtering, two-stage validation, and some tool integration together.
Filtering can discard weakly described but relevant pages, and isolated validation can still ratify a flawed step.
Open-model comparisons use unmatched models, tools, and reporting conventions.
Search/browser/tool/validator call counts, training compute, and dollars are missing.
The 8B result mixes SFT, GRPO, teacher actions, rubrics, and the NIS harness.
